A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same convex ReLU approximation and private optimization study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original MNIST and FashionMNIST experiments, with additional private and non-private MNIST experiments in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: Section 6 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including private hyperparameter-tuning results. Appendices E and I also contain original MNIST and FashionMNIST results.

M1.justification: The convex objective, random hyperplane construction and inference rule in Section 3 remain unchanged. Section 5 adds a private best-of-K hyperparameter-selection procedure with Poisson-distributed K and calibrates NoisyCGD regularization to match base-model privacy, extending the training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 classification from raw, vectorized 32×32 color images, substantially extending the earlier grayscale MNIST and FashionMNIST coverage to natural images. Both earlier datasets remain evaluated; FashionMNIST moves to Appendix I.

E2.justification: v2 adds learning-rate-tuned, DP-SGD-trained logistic regression to the MNIST comparison in Figure 2 and the new CIFAR-10 comparison in Figure 3. The original three model/optimizer combinations remain. Tempered-sigmoid networks are discussed but not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 changes the stated DP-SGD sampling protocol from fixed-size sampling without replacement to Poisson sampling. v2 replaces the fixed NoisyCGD learning-rate/regularization product with privacy-matched calibration and expands model-width tuning. It also adds privacy-accounted selection with K distributed as Poisson(20). The 400-epoch budget, batch-size parameter 1000 and noise scales 5 and 15 remain.

E4.justification: Figure 1 revises the sensitivity comparison for the learning-rate/regularization product: 5.4×10^-5 replaces 4×10^-4, while 10^-4 and 2×10^-4 remain. The hyperplane-count analyses in Figures 4–5 and the PLD-versus-RDP comparison in Figure 6 are retained, despite appendix reorganization.

E5.justification: v1 already displays error bars but does not specify their meaning or trial count. Section 6.2 of v2 states that the main and FashionMNIST results average five trials, with bars representing ±1.96 standard errors; Tables 1–2 also report five-run means. This newly discloses statistical practices without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds tuning-inclusive results and CIFAR-10 findings. At ε=2.88, Tables 1–2 report NoisyCGD-convex, DP-SGD-convex and DP-SGD-ReLU accuracies of 0.927/0.929/0.916 on MNIST and 0.416/0.417/0.427 on CIFAR-10. NoisyCGD curves also change in MNIST and retained FashionMNIST comparisons. These are added or revised results under changed protocols, not established same-setting gains. Figures 4–6 retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the without-replacement amplification lemma and privacy-profile construction with a Poisson-sampling bound. Section 5 adds Theorem 5.1 and accompanying reasoning for private randomized model selection. Appendix D adds an explicit proof of the retained random-data utility corollary. The original convexification and principal utility results remain.

C1.justification: The central claim of achieving ReLU-comparable privacy–utility through convex approximation remains. v2 adds privacy-accounted hyperparameter tuning to its stated contributions and broadens its novelty framing from high-utility NoisyCGD results to high-utility benchmark results under hidden-state privacy analysis generally.

C2.justification: v2 adds a dimensionality-versus-DP-noise explanation for the hyperplane-count choice and acknowledges that tempered-sigmoid baselines could perform better. It removes v1's suggestion that private benefits specifically arise from convexification rather than approximation. The explicit compute/memory limitation disappears from the conclusion, although Appendix H mentions memory-constrained grids.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies explicit, finite, dataset-specific hyperplane and hidden-width grids and the learning-rate range, replacing less complete search descriptions. It explains the GPU-memory constraint on those grids. Section 6 also documents using vectorized CIFAR-10 images without pretrained convolutional features.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around private hyperparameter selection, adding Papernot and Steinke and Koskela et al.; Poisson accounting, adding Lebeda et al.; and newer nonconvex optimization rates, adding Arora et al. and Lowy et al. It explicitly positions logistic regression as the strongest prior hidden-state application and removes several earlier motivation citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with an explicit contribution list and hidden-state framing. Theory is condensed and redistributed to appendices; experiments are reorganized into tuning-inclusive and best-model comparisons. The two MNIST approximation appendices are merged into subsections. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds two comparison tables and a paired CIFAR-10 figure, incorporates logistic-regression curves into Figure 2, and revises axes and legends. FashionMNIST is revised and moved from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 7. Retained appendix figures are resized and reflowed, substantially changing the experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: The private-tuning analysis and cost-inclusive tables address v1's omission of model-selection privacy costs. Logistic-regression comparisons and CIFAR-10 experiments substantially strengthen evidence for the hidden-state application, while explicit grids and uncertainty definitions improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the reduced compute/memory discussion and reporting inconsistencies, notably the apparent reversal of the noise-to-ε association in Section 6.1.
